case_name: G. Ramamoorthy vs The State Of Karnataka

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Karnataka and Ms. Sandhya Mahesh

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Marriage between son of the petitioner and respondent came to be solemnized on 31.05.2012. Respondent filed a petition for divorce and lodged a complaint against the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: A complaint cannot be read in isolation and has to be read along with allegations made in other related complaints.
legal_principles.held: averments made in the complaint cannot be read in isolation and it has to be read along with allegations made in M.C.No.448/2014

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to quash a FIR to show that it is false and has been filed with mala fide intentions.
legal_principles.held: He would also contend that all overt-acts alleged to have been made by petitioner has taken place at Ambur, Vellore District, Bengaluru and as such, false complaint against the petitioner has been filed at Bengaluru by concealing material facts only to harass the petitioner
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

outcome.final_order: The FIR registered against the petitioner/accused No.2 is quashed.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
